This glossary gives a concise first definition for terms used across the site. It does not replace canonical concept pages: follow the links for deeper explanations where available.

## Language models and generation

- **Language model** — a model that assigns probabilities to text sequences or their next tokens, conditional on context. See the [LLM panorama](llm-overview.qmd).
- **Generative model** — a model that defines a distribution from which new samples can be produced, possibly conditioned on an input; it is not necessarily a language model.
- **LLM (*large language model*)** — a language model trained at large scale. No universal parameter threshold defines this category; see [scaling laws](scaling-laws.qmd).
- **Scaling law** — an empirical relationship between a training resource (parameters, data, or compute) and a measure such as loss; it depends on the regime studied and does not establish a universal LLM threshold. See [scaling laws](scaling-laws.qmd).

## Text and data

- **Token** — a discrete unit processed by a model; it may be a word, subword, character, or another segment.
- **Tokenization** — converting text into a sequence of token IDs.
- **Vocabulary** — the set of tokens a tokenizer can represent.
- **Prefix** — the part of a sequence already available to condition the next prediction.
- **Forward pass** — the network computation that transforms the context into representations and logits while keeping model parameters fixed. See [GPT and Transformers](transformer.qmd).
- **Decoding** — the procedure that uses logits or their distribution to select the next token; it follows the forward pass and is one step in generation. Do not confuse it with a **decoder**, a component of some Transformer architectures. See [Generating text](generation.qmd).
- **Autoregressive generation** — an iterative process that selects a token, appends it to the context, and repeats until a stopping condition is met. See [Generating text](generation.qmd).
- **Prefill** — the inference phase that processes the initial prompt as a sequence and produces the logits used for the first generated-token choice; it may also populate a KV cache. See [Generating text](generation.qmd).
- **Decode phase** — the iterative inference phase that processes newly generated tokens to obtain subsequent predictions. Do not confuse it with **decoding**, the token-selection procedure. See [Generating text](generation.qmd).
- **Context window** — the amount of token context a model can process in a given input.

## Representations and geometry

- **Embedding** — a vector representation of an object. The term refers to different objects depending on context; the entries below distinguish the main cases. See [embedding space](embedding-space.qmd).
- **Initial token embedding** — the vector retrieved from the embedding matrix using a token ID; before contextualization, the same ID selects the same vector regardless of the surrounding sentence. See [embedding space](embedding-space.qmd).
- **Contextualized representation** — the vector produced by the network for a given position after taking context into account; unlike the initial embedding, it depends on the other accessible tokens and the model's transformations. See [contextualized representations](contextualized-representations.qmd).
- **Sentence or document embedding** — a vector representing an entire text, obtained from an encoder or an aggregation method; it should not be conflated with an initial token embedding or the hidden state of a single position. See [cosine similarity](cosine-similarity.qmd).
- **Embedding space** — the vector space in which object representations are compared; its geometry depends on the model, layer, and representation method. See [embedding space](embedding-space.qmd).
- **Cosine similarity** — the cosine of the angle between two non-zero vectors; see its [definition, assumptions, and limitations](cosine-similarity.qmd).
- **Anisotropy** — a vector distribution that favours some directions in the space; it can affect scores and nearest-neighbour rankings.
- **Hubness** — a phenomenon in which some points become the nearest neighbours of many other points.
- **Linear representation hypothesis** — a family of hypotheses that features may correspond to directions or subspaces in activations; see [representation linearity](embedding-linearity.qmd).

These topics are grouped in the [Representation geometry and interpretability](embedding-space.qmd) path.

## Probability and learning

- **Logit** — an unnormalized real-valued score for a class or token. See [Logits](logits.qmd).
- **Softmax** — a transformation of scores into positive probabilities that sum to one. See [Probabilities](probabilities.qmd).
- **Likelihood** — the probability assigned to observations by a parameterized model, viewed as a function of its parameters. See [Likelihood](likelihood.qmd).
- **Shannon entropy** — the average uncertainty of a discrete variable under its distribution. See [Entropy](entropy.qmd).
- **Cross-entropy** — the average cost associated with a target distribution and a predictive distribution. See [Cross-entropy and KL divergence](cross-entropy.qmd).
- **KL divergence** — a measure of discrepancy between distributions that is generally asymmetric. See [Cross-entropy and KL divergence](cross-entropy.qmd).
- **Loss function** — the numerical objective optimized during training; it is not a universal measure of quality. See [Loss](loss.qmd).
- **Teacher forcing** — a training-time conditioning strategy in which each next-token prediction uses the ground-truth preceding tokens rather than previously sampled model outputs. See [training examples](training-examples.qmd).
- **Exposure bias** — a possible mismatch between ground-truth prefixes used during teacher-forced training and model-generated prefixes encountered at inference; its practical impact is task- and protocol-dependent. See [training examples](training-examples.qmd).
- **Gradient** — a derivative of an objective with respect to a variable or parameter. See [Gradients](gradients.qmd).
- **Calibration** — empirical agreement between predicted probabilities and observed frequencies for comparable events.

## Transformer architecture

- **Depth** — the number of Transformer blocks stacked in the network. See [GPT and Transformers](transformer.qmd).
- **Width** — a term often used for the dimension of representations flowing between blocks (`d_model` or *hidden size* in a classic GPT); its meaning depends on context and should not be conflated with `d_ff` or `d_head`. See [GPT and Transformers](transformer.qmd).
- **Hidden size** — the dimension of an internal representation vector; in classic GPT models, it usually corresponds to `d_model`, the residual-stream width.
- **Transformer** — a family of neural architectures built around attention and representation transformations, introduced by Vaswani and colleagues in 2017. The term does not name a single model family. See the [Transformer overview](transformer.qmd) and [history](transformer-history.qmd).
- **GPT (*Generative Pre-trained Transformer*)** — a family of pretrained generative models built on Transformers; classic GPT models use a decoder-only architecture and an autoregressive objective. GPT is not synonymous with Transformer. See [GPT and Transformer](transformer.qmd) and [Transformer architectures](transformer-architectures.qmd).
- **Attention** — a mechanism that computes weights from queries and keys, then aggregates the corresponding values. See [Q, K, and V](queries-keys-values.qmd).
- **Query (Q)** — a projection used to compute compatibility scores with keys. See [Q, K, and V](queries-keys-values.qmd).
- **Key (K)** — a projection compared with a query to produce a score. See [Q, K, and V](queries-keys-values.qmd).
- **Value (V)** — a projection whose representations are aggregated using attention weights. See [Q, K, and V](queries-keys-values.qmd).
- **Self-attention** — attention where queries, keys, and values are derived from representations of the same sequence. See [Q, K, and V](queries-keys-values.qmd).
- **Multi-head attention** — several attention mechanisms computed in parallel and then combined.
- **Causal mask** — a constraint preventing a position from accessing future positions. See [Causal masking](causal-masking.qmd).
- **Autoregressive Transformer** — a Transformer trained to model a sequence from left to right, predicting each token conditioned on earlier tokens. “Autoregressive” describes the prediction objective; it does not require generating only one token at a time during training.
- **Encoder** — a component that builds contextual representations of an input; in BERT, for example, attention can use context from both directions.
- **Decoder** — a component designed to produce outputs from context; in an autoregressive decoder, a causal mask prevents access to future tokens.
- **Tensor** — an array of numbers organized along several axes. Its shape indicates the size of each axis; it does not by itself specify the meaning of the data. See [Tensors](tensors.qmd).
- **Positional encoding / position information** — a mechanism that supplies the model with information about token order. Approaches include absolute encodings, relative biases, and RoPE. See [positional encoding and RoPE](positional-encoding.qmd).
- **RoPE (*Rotary Position Embedding*)** — a positional encoding that applies position-dependent rotations to coordinate pairs of queries and keys.
- **Parameter** — a value learned during training.
- **Fine-tuning** — continuing training of a pretrained model on a particular objective or dataset.
- **Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)** — adaptation on curated input–target or instruction–response demonstrations.
- **RLHF (*reinforcement learning from human feedback*)** — a family of post-training methods that use human preferences; a classic pipeline trains a reward model from comparisons and optimizes a policy against it.
- **Reward model** — a model trained to score responses in a way that reflects preference data; its scores are learned proxies, not objective measures of truth or quality.
- **PPO (*proximal policy optimization*)** — a policy-gradient reinforcement-learning algorithm used in some RLHF pipelines to optimize a policy while constraining update size.
- **DPO (*direct preference optimization*)** — a method that optimizes a policy directly from preference comparisons, without the separate reward-model-plus-PPO loop of the classic RLHF recipe.
- **GRPO (*group relative policy optimization*)** — a policy-optimization method that compares rewards across several sampled responses to the same prompt to form a relative learning signal. The reward may come from a verifier or another evaluator; GRPO does not specify its source.
- **RLVR (*reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards*)** — reinforcement learning in which rewards are computed from checkable outcomes, such as exact answers, executable tests, or output-format validation.
